title: Oversized or too-deeply-nested SQL is silently half-parsed instead of rejected
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

sqlparse has limits on grouping depth/token count meant to protect against DoS, but exceeding them is silently ignored.

    import sqlparse
    sql = "SELECT " + "(" * 200 + "1" + ")" * 200
    sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True)
EXPECTED: raises sqlparse.exceptions.SQLParseError with a message containing "Maximum grouping depth exceeded".
ACTUAL: returns a formatted string with no error.

Similar inputs are probably affected too; please fix the underlying problem rather than just this case.
acceptance: The nested example raises SQLParseError mentioning "Maximum grouping depth exceeded"
